correctness.rationale: The Kneser diameter-two rule is valid for every n>=5, including the Petersen boundary. Intersecting target pairs fail separation iff the two differing endpoints form two isolates or an isolated K2. Disjoint targets fail iff the four endpoints are edge-closed and admit a balanced bipartition with no selected within-side edges; after the first obstructions, precisely P3 plus isolate, P4 and C4 are possible. The if-and-only-if is exhaustive. At p=(log n+c)/n, isolated-vertex factorial moments converge to Poisson(e^{-c}), while expected numbers of components of orders 2, 3, 4 vanish using a spanning-tree union bound. Monotonicity extends the fixed-c result to drifting windows. The independent C++ direct-distance checker agreed on 2130944 exhaustive small cases and 150000 reproducible random cases; the proof does not infer infinite truth from finite checks.

originality.rationale: The claim is the exact four-component characterization of every metric resolving probe set of KG(n,2), plus its distinct random-critical Poisson tail. The inspected closest primary literature establishes metric-dimension scalars, broad intersection equivalences and hypergraph detectability but does not state or imply the exact classified obstruction list or the specific critical-window probability without nontrivial additional structural argument. Six actual semantic database searches, targeted general-literature searches and primary full-text inspections located no dominating theorem. This is self-review best-knowledge originality only, with stated residual risk.
residual_risks: A previous exact component characterization might be hidden in an unindexed or inaccessible journal article, thesis, appendix, or equivalent Johnson-graph formulation.

The general 2013 intersection condition is a close logical predecessor; originality depends specifically on the explicit exact component list and new random asymptotic, not on inventing the generic resolving test.
The zero-one threshold for isolates is classical; only the distinct Kneser application and nontrivial one-isolate survival law are claimed as new.
No independent bibliographic or scientific audit has been performed.

value.rationale: A natural distance-transitive graph has a full recognizing characterization of every resolving landmark set, not merely a known metric dimension. The four small ground-component obstructions permit linear-time membership recognition and reveal the exact sharp random sensor density and critical-window reliability e^{-e^{-c}}(1+e^{-c}). This is a genuine global structural lemma and motivated asymptotic network observability statistic, rather than a routine parameter recomputation. It demonstrates that one ground isolate is tolerable even though ordinary random-graph connectivity forbids all isolates.
